about.title: Barstow Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Barstow sits at a crossroads of freight, retail, and daily life, where everything from warehouse equipment along I-15 to household goods sold on W Main Street and E Main Street passes through the community. When a product fails, whether it's a defective vehicle part, a malfunctioning appliance, or a tool with a missing warning label, the resulting injury can upend a family's routine fast. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a claim under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was defective, not on proving the manufacturer was careless. We offer a free consultation to review what happened and explain your possible next steps. If a product caused your injury, keeping it exactly as it was at the time can matter, and reaching out early costs nothing.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or batteries
Lacerations from defective tools or machinery parts
Crush injuries from failing vehicle components
Traumatic brain injuries from faulty safety equipment
Poisoning or chemical exposure from mislabeled products
Fractures from collapsing furniture or equipment

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Path Forward
items.desc: California generally lets injured people focus on whether the product was defective rather than proving the maker was negligent. We can help identify whether a design, manufacturing, or warning defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the product can potentially be held accountable. We can help sort out which parties were involved in getting the product into your hands.

items.title: The Product Itself Matters as Evidence
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact, without repairs or alterations, can be important to any future claim. We can advise on preserving it properly.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, which generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused harm. We can look at the specifics of your case and explain what applies.

items.question: What if I bought the product from a small shop on Main Street instead of the manufacturer?
items.answer: Retailers can sometimes share liability along with manufacturers and distributors, depending on the circumstances. We can help figure out which parties in the chain may be involved.

items.question: Does your firm charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews. We typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
